text:
Vegas won this one on the scoreboard and on the ice, which makes it a rare night where the 5-2 final understates the gap only a little. VGK created 4.10 expected goals to CHI's 2.01 and got 72% of simulated replays, and the lead came from steady pressure rather than luck. The one soft spot was the opening goal: Victor Olofsson scored on the power play from a 5% chance at 10:30 of the first, and Trevor Connelly's tip-in made it 2-0 before the period ended.

CHI never went away. Jordan Greenway, who put five shots on goal, pulled them within one in the second on a 6% wrister, and Patrick Kane did it again early in the third to make it 2-3. Jack Eichel answered the first one in under three minutes with a 34% snap shot, and Noah Hanifin restored the two-goal margin 39 seconds after Kane scored. Those quick replies kept CHI from building any momentum. Spencer Knight faced 36 shots and allowed four goals on 3.30 expected, a 0.70 shortfall.

Mark Stone's slap shot at 17:27 of the third, a 79% chance, sealed it. Eichel finished with a goal and two assists, and Shea Theodore and Brayden McNabb each added two assists while their pairs controlled the chance count, with on-ice expected goals of 2.31 to 0.45 and 1.98 to 0.45. VGK also won 33 of 58 faceoffs and outhit CHI 23 to 14. Carter Hart stopped 24 of 26, almost exactly what the chances called for.
